values.note: 2026 Brower Park: water + electric site $35 Mon-Thu, $40 Fri-Sun, $50 holiday/event; prime water + electric $40 / $45 / $55. One rate for everyone (no resident discount stated). Seasonal $2,800 ($2,900 with seepage pit, $3,700 prime). A vehicle permit is required on top of camping: $10 a day at Brower, or an annual county permit $35. $5 non-refundable processing fee per site reserved.

fees.source: https://www.mecostacountyparks.com/uploads/9/2/6/3/92633552/2026_rate_card.pdf ('2026 RATES Brower Park Camping Mon-Thurs $35 - $40, Fri-Sun $40 - $45, Holiday/Event $50 - $55'; 'Annual Vehicle Permit $35') + https://www.mecostacountyparks.com/rules-rates--cancellations.html (Brower tab: 'Water + Electric $35 $40 $50', 'Prime: Water + Electric $40 $45 $55'; 'Daily Vehicle Permit - Brower & School Section $10 per day'; 'Vehicle permits are required for park entrance and in addition to camping fees at the following parks: Brower Park') + online-reservations.html ('There is a $5 non-refundable processing fee per individual campsite'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: 230 campsites (120 of them seasonal, let by lottery each season) plus 10 cabins; all sites have electric and a water outlet; 'prime' water/electric sites cost more.

note: Mecosta County park on the Muskegon River / Hardy Pond backwaters (23056 Polk Rd): 280 wooded acres with almost 8,000 ft of river frontage, a 1,000-ft sandy beach and boat launches on both shores. Day-use area and launch open year-round. --Claude
summary: County pages: 2026 $35 (W/E weekday) to $55 (prime, holiday), $5 per-site processing fee, plus a required $10/day Brower vehicle permit ($35 annual); 230 sites (120 seasonal by lottery, 52%) + 10 cabins, electric and water outlet at every site; showers, flush toilets, dump; 2027 season April 23 - October 10; reservable online through GoingToCamp (2-night minimum, 3 on holidays, already recorded 2026-10-12). Amperage, sewer and rig lengths not stated. Note cleaned of site/hookup/booking text and the MINIMUM STAY line (booking.min_stay holds it).
flags: Website: the second link https://reserve.mecostacountyparks.com/brower/campsites no longer resolves; the county now books through https://mecostacounty.goingtocamp.com/ (linked from https://www.mecostacountyparks.com/online-reservations.html).
Seasonal share: 120 of 230 campsites (52%) are seasonal, let by lottery; the other ~110 sell nightly (2-night minimum), so long-stay test 4 passes.
